# Security & Privacy Requirements Quality Checklist: Community Detection Framework

**Purpose**: Validate that security, privacy, data protection, and safety requirements are complete, consistent, measurable, and aligned with the constitution
**Created**: 2026-09-03
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Zero-Trust Logging & Data Protection

- [x] CHK001 Is the zero-trust logging posture (FR-030) specified with a complete enumeration of protected data types: graph data, node identifiers, and topology information? [Completeness, FR-030]
- [x] CHK002 Are the logging tiers (error, warn, info, debug, trace) specified with their exact scope and the conditions under which each tier is active? [Completeness, FR-030]
- [x] CHK003 Is the opt-in logging mechanism specified: how users enable granular logging, what configuration controls exist, and the default state (disabled)? [Clarity, FR-030]
- [x] CHK004 Is the requirement that protected data MUST NOT appear in any log tier unless explicitly enabled specified as a verifiable constraint? [Measurability, FR-030]
- [x] CHK005 Are the success criteria for zero-trust logging (SC-015) specified with a testable verification methodology? [Measurability, SC-015]
- [x] CHK006 Is the distinction between "base observability" events (algorithm phase transitions) and "graph data" specified clearly? Are phase events considered safe to log? [Clarity, FR-030/FR-017]
- [x] CHK007 Are requirements specified for log output destinations (stdout, file, tracing subscriber) and any sanitization requirements per destination? [Completeness, FR-036]

## Memory Safety & Unsafe Code

- [x] CHK008 Is the zero-unsafe-code policy (Constitution Principle IV) reflected in requirements: are there any exceptions or is it an absolute constraint? [Consistency, FR-038]
- [x] CHK009 Is the formal justification RFC process for unsafe code specified with its criteria and approval requirements? [Clarity, FR-038]
- [x] CHK010 Are requirements specified for how unsafe code (if any) MUST be isolated and documented? [Completeness, FR-038]
- [x] CHK011 Is the relationship between the zero-unsafe policy and external crate dependencies (e.g., rayon, petgraph) specified? Are dependency safety requirements defined? [Clarity, FR-038]

## Panic Safety & Error Handling

- [x] CHK012 Is the zero-panic requirement (Constitution Principle IV) reflected in the API contracts: are all public APIs specified as returning `Result` for fallible operations? [Consistency, Gap]
- [x] CHK013 Are the `clippy::unwrap_used`, `clippy::expect_used`, `clippy::panic` deny attributes reflected as requirements for all library crates? [Consistency, Constitution IV]
- [x] CHK014 Is the error handling contract specified for all failure modes: invalid input, algorithm failure, resource exhaustion, and internal invariants? [Completeness, Gap]
- [x] CHK015 Are the domain error types specified with sufficient granularity to enable programmatic error recovery by callers? [Clarity, Gap]
- [x] CHK016 Is the `clippy::todo` and `clippy::unimplemented` deny requirement reflected as a constraint on incomplete functionality in production code? [Consistency, Constitution IV]

## Input Validation & Graph Integrity

- [x] CHK017 Is the negative weight validation requirement (FR-032) specified with the default behavior (reject at input) AND the opt-out mechanism (defer to execution)? [Clarity, FR-032]
- [x] CHK018 Is the graph validation requirement specified with a complete list of validation checks: non-negative weights, CSR structure integrity, and any others? [Completeness, Gap]
- [x] CHK019 Is the `validate_on_construction` flag behavior specified for both graph builders and algorithm configs? [Clarity, FR-027]
- [x] CHK020 Are requirements specified for handling malformed input in file parsers (EdgeList, JSON, GML): error types, error messages, and recovery behavior? [Completeness, FR-039]
- [x] CHK021 Is the zero-weight edge requirement (FR-024) specified with the guarantee of no division-by-zero, and is this verifiable? [Measurability, FR-024]
- [x] CHK022 Is the self-loop handling requirement (FR-025) specified with guarantees against infinite loops in degree calculations? [Clarity, FR-025]

## WebAssembly Security

- [x] CHK023 Are security requirements specified for the WASM deployment: memory isolation, sandboxing boundaries, and input sanitization? [Completeness, FR-037]
- [x] CHK024 Is the WASM single-threaded execution constraint specified as a security requirement or a performance limitation? [Clarity, Assumption]
- [x] CHK025 Are requirements specified for WASM memory management: how graph data is passed across the JS boundary and memory cleanup? [Completeness, FR-037]
- [x] CHK026 Is the WASM build algorithm restriction (Leiden + Louvain only) specified with the security or performance rationale? [Clarity, Assumption]

## Algorithm Safety & Termination

- [x] CHK027 Is the termination guarantee (FR-026) specified as a safety requirement: all algorithms MUST terminate via convergence or iteration bound? [Clarity, FR-026]
- [x] CHK028 Is the maximum iteration bound specified with its default value and configuration mechanism? [Completeness, FR-026]
- [x] CHK029 Is the deterministic tie-breaking requirement (FR-026) specified to prevent infinite oscillation in bipartite/cyclic graphs? [Clarity, FR-026]
- [x] CHK030 Are requirements specified for detecting and handling degenerate graph inputs that could cause non-termination or incorrect results? [Coverage, FR-035]

## Licensing & Third-Party Attribution

- [x] CHK031 Is the dual-licensing requirement (MIT OR Apache-2.0) specified with the mechanism for license selection by downstream users? [Clarity, Constitution VII]
- [x] CHK032 Is the third-party attribution requirement specified: which upstream projects require notices, and where are they documented? [Completeness, Constitution VII]
- [x] CHK033 Is the `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` file specified with its required contents and maintenance requirements? [Completeness, Constitution VII]
- [x] CHK034 Are license compatibility requirements specified for external dependencies (petgraph, rayon, etc.)? [Clarity, Gap]

## Observability Overhead & Resource Bounds

- [x] CHK035 Is the 20% observability overhead budget (SC-013) specified as a hard requirement or a target? What happens if exceeded? [Clarity, SC-013]
- [x] CHK036 Is the overhead measurement methodology specified: baseline definition, measurement conditions, and pass/fail criteria? [Measurability, SC-013]
- [x] CHK037 Are memory usage requirements specified: is the "graphs fit in system memory" assumption a hard constraint or a soft target? [Clarity, Assumption]
- [x] CHK038 Is the out-of-core processing exclusion specified as a scope boundary, and are there requirements for graceful failure when memory is exhausted? [Clarity, Assumption]

## Testing & Verification Safety

- [x] CHK039 Are property-based testing requirements (Constitution Principle VI) specified with the invariants that MUST be verified for each algorithm? [Completeness, spec Property-Based Testing section]
- [x] CHK040 Is the ground-truth validation requirement (SC-003, SC-004) specified with the reference data sourcing and acceptance thresholds? [Completeness, SC-003/SC-004]
- [x] CHK041 Are the SNAP dataset regression testing requirements specified with the expected outcomes and failure criteria? [Completeness, SC-003/Constitution VI]
- [x] CHK042 Is the connected communities invariant (SC-001) specified as a mandatory property test for all algorithms, not just Leiden? [Clarity, SC-001]

## Security Consistency & Conflicts

- [x] CHK043 Is the zero-trust logging requirement (FR-030) consistent with the observability requirements (FR-017)? Can full observability be achieved without leaking graph data? [Consistency, FR-030/FR-017]
- [x] CHK044 Is the deterministic seed requirement (FR-007) consistent across all algorithms, or are there algorithms where determinism is not achievable? [Consistency, FR-007]
- [x] CHK045 Is the WASM single-threaded constraint consistent with the rayon dependency for parallelism? Is the fallback behavior specified? [Consistency, Assumption]
- [x] CHK046 Are the `clippy::allow_attributes_without_reason` deny requirements consistent with procedural macro usage in dependencies? [Consistency, Gap]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
